title: ANDS Studio — Overall impression
walkthrough:
A yellow banner runs across the top of every page: "Demo / evaluation environment — nothing here is transmitted to Health Canada and no email is sent." Below sits a top bar branded "ANDS Studio · guided ANDS filing," beside a nav of icon-labelled chips — "Journey," "Dossiers," "Portfolio," "Registry," "Correspondence," "Help" — each with a hover tooltip. The active route is highlighted; a user chip sits at the far right. First-time visitors may see a dismissible "What you'll do here" primer tagged "New to ANDS? Start here." With no prior session the hero shows; a one-time external-prerequisites checklist can appear first.

The headline reads "File your ANDS with Health Canada — guided end to end." The body states an Abbreviated New Drug Submission is one of the most complex filings a company can make and that this walks you through it step by step, every term in plain language, the right pathway chosen, and readiness visible throughout. The primary button is "Start my submission →." Two chips below read "Managing several products? Open the dossier catalog →" (with a count) and "Portfolio roll-up →" (with an in-progress count). A line notes bilingual Module 1 and Product Monograph (EN + FR) status live inside each dossier.

A "Trust & security" strip follows, headed "the questions your auditor asks first — answered plainly." It lists four live pillars — Data residency ("Self-hosted — can stay in Canada"), Tenant isolation ("Per-client data walls, refused at the API"), Roles & segregation of duties ("Scoped roles: who can create / archive / sign"), and Audit-trail tamper controls ("Append-only, actor + UTC stamped, exportable") — plus a fifth marked with a "roadmap" chip, "SOC 2 / SSO / SCIM" ("On the roadmap — not certified / not built yet"). A "One-page security summary" button expands honest per-pillar detail. A quieter footnote reads "Grounded in real Health Canada process · your progress is saved automatically."

Starting opens a three-column layout: a journey step rail, the active step's card, and a right panel with a "submission tower" of module tiles plus a readiness card. The top bar gains a readiness chip — "Ready to file" or a percentage — and a "Reset session" button, which opens a modal requiring you to type "RESET" and states plainly that this only detaches the local session; the dossier and its append-only Part-11 audit trail remain re-openable. When a dossier is attached, an "Audit trail" card points to the immutable who/what/when ledger, exportable as CSV.

Help opens a "Regulatory reference" page: the primary Health Canada sources behind everything the app checks, every finding linking to one, all links to canada.ca or laws-lois.justice.gc.ca. Cards group under "Filing an ANDS," "Generic-specific," and "Transmitting & after approval." A "How validation works here" section lists rule-ID families (CA-E-1xxx–4xxx, an XML backbone, PDF conformance, and CA-REP-0001, which blocks filing while a placeholder ID is in use) and pulls the complete rule catalogue live from the engine into per-family lists. A "How AI drafting is controlled" section states drafting is opt-in per ✦AI section, nothing saves until "Use this draft," every AI-assisted document is permanently labelled and audit-recorded, and the human review plus e-signature gate still stands.

The Roadmap page states plainly that anything listed is not available today, each card naming a capability, a "Target" chip marked "in design" or "planned," and a short detail, with a "← Back to sign in" link.
